sections.h2: Which Union County offices handle property tax?
sections.html:
Union County keeps its tax offices together at the County Office Building, 233 West Sixth Street, Marysville, Ohio 43040. Three of them matter to a seller.

  • Auditor. Sets values, keeps the tax credits, runs the Board of Revision complaint process and stamps deeds. Phone 937-645-3003.
  • Treasurer. Sends bills and collects payment; a drop box sits at the rear entrance. Phone 937-645-3035, open weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., closed on federal holidays.
  • Recorder. Files the deed and any mortgage release after the auditor's stamp. Phone 937-645-3032.

The auditor's page puts the county at about 32,800 property records, and the treasurer's page describes more than 30,000 parcels. By the treasurer's account, roughly 70 percent of what the office collects goes to local schools.

sections.h2: How does Union County calculate a property tax bill?
sections.html:
Each parcel gets a market value from the auditor, and the treasurer's FAQ puts assessed value at 35 percent of it. The assessed value is multiplied by the total tax rate for the parcel's district, then reduced by credits.

  • Residential and agricultural property gets a 10 percent credit on the net tax for levies passed before November 2013.
  • Owner-occupied homes qualify for an added 2 1/2 percent credit covering the house and up to an acre of land, after the owner applies with form DTE 105C.
  • Levies passed after November 2013 that raise funding do not carry the rollbacks.
  • Owners who are 65 or older, or permanently disabled, can claim the Homestead Exemption, which has carried an income test since 2014.

Ohio caps unvoted taxation at ten mills per thousand dollars of assessed value, and any levy beyond that needs a vote. The county's tax rate page lists rates by district and levy, and the DTE 515 report gives the composite reduction factors. To see your rate, find the parcel on the auditor's website and follow the “Where your taxes go” link. The first two digits of the parcel number identify the tax district.

Where a house sits matters for schools. The auditor's GIS notes that when a district line crosses a house, the school district where the master bedroom is located governs the whole house.

sections.h2: What are the Union County due dates and penalties?
sections.html:
Bills are mailed in January and June, and Ohio collects a year behind. A bill that arrives in 2026 covers tax year 2025. The county sets each year's dates, and the treasurer's FAQ says the first half usually falls in mid-February and the second half in mid-July or August. The county's 2026 schedule is below.

Union County treasurer calendar for 2025 taxes payable in 2026
DateWhat happened or applies
February 18, 2026First half due
February 19 and 28, 20265 percent, then 10 percent penalty added to unpaid first half
August 12, 2026Second half due
August 13 and 22, 20265 percent, then 10 percent penalty added to unpaid 2025 tax
September 1, 20264.67 percent interest on unpaid prior years' delinquency
December 1, 20262.33 percent interest on the total unpaid balance

Source: Union County Treasurer payment information.

A U.S. Postal Service postmark dated on the due date is timely, and a postage meter stamp from a private machine is not. The county also says a missing bill never excuses a late payment. Before the second half came due in 2026, the treasurer advised paying only the first half, because House Bill 186 required rates to be recalculated for the second half. The treasurer said overpayments would be credited or refunded.

sections.h2: How do you pay a Union County tax bill, or spread it out?
sections.html:
Checks go to the Union County Treasurer at the Sixth Street address, by mail, in person or in the back drop box. The county takes cards and e-checks online, and the treasurer's FAQ says a processing fee goes to the payment vendor rather than the county. In 2026 the treasurer also accepted payments at a Richwood bank on set days before each due date, so check the payment information page for any such location.

Two programs help with budgeting:

  • Real Estate Tax Escrow Program. Prepay by the month, and the treasurer applies the funds as each half comes due.
  • Delinquent payment plan. A written contract with the treasurer lets you pay back taxes in installments while keeping current tax paid. Penalty and interest are held in escrow and removed once the contract is paid off, and added back if you default.

Unpaid bills draw a delinquent notice in late September or early October, and the owner's name is printed in the paper's delinquent list. When tax is still owed the following November, the file goes to the county prosecutor to begin foreclosure.

sections.h2: How do you challenge a Union County valuation?
sections.html:
The auditor receives each complaint and passes it to the Board of Revision. Under Ohio Revised Code 5715.19, the deadline is the later of March 31 or the end of first-half collection. The auditor's FAQ describes a filing period that opens January 1 and closes March 31 of the year after the tax year.

  • File a notarized DTE Form 1 by email, fax or mail to the Auditor's Office, Attn: Board of Revision, at the Sixth Street address.
  • Contest only the current tax year. The board does not look back.
  • Attach a closing statement, purchase contract, escrow statement and deed if you bought or sold recently.
  • Hearing dates follow the order in which complaints are received.
  • A property held by a business or trust should use an attorney. An individual does not need one.

If the change you seek tops $50,000 in market value (or $17,500 assessed), the school board is notified. Board decisions are held for 30 days, and a refund or credit follows about sixty days after that. To appeal a ruling, use DTE Form 4 with the Ohio Board of Tax Appeals or go to the Court of Common Pleas, in either case within 30 days of the decision letter. In many cases a decision holds until the next triennial update. The auditor reports the last full reappraisal in 2019, with updates every third year after.

sections.h2: What tax relief programs does Union County offer?
sections.html:
Besides the rollbacks above, the auditor administers two programs that a buyer or seller may ask about.

  • Homestead Exemption. The county page lists age 65 or older, permanent disability, or a surviving spouse aged 59 to 64 of a person already receiving the exemption. Applicants must own and occupy the house, and the application is due the first Monday in June. Disabled veterans use form DTE 105I. Ask the auditor for the current income cap.
  • Current Agricultural Use Value (CAUV). Land of at least ten acres worked commercially for three years can be taxed on what it earns as farmland. A parcel under ten acres needs $2,500 average yearly gross income. The auditor must receive the application between the first Monday of January and the first Monday of March. Pulling out of the program triggers a charge equal to the previous three years of tax savings.

When a property sells, section 319.202 asks the grantee to affirm whether the seller said the property carried a rollback or CAUV status. A seller with CAUV land should talk to the auditor before closing about the recoupment charge.

sections.h2: How does property tax work at a Union County closing?
sections.html:
The settlement statement normally prorates the tax, which ends the seller's responsibility for later bills. The treasurer's FAQ tells a seller who still receives a bill to hand it to the new owner or phone the office, so a corrected bill can go out. Look at the settlement statement, since a bill for the prior year can come due after you have moved.

The county is growing quickly. In Census Bureau figures, the county reached an estimated 73,446 residents in 2025, a 17.0 percent rise on the 2020 base. The typical owned home is valued at $344,900, and 968 building permits were issued in 2025. Marysville Exempted Village, Fairbanks, North Union, Triad, Jonathan Alder, Buckeye Valley, Elgin, Benjamin Logan and Dublin City serve the county's school districts.

Have the title company check for current or delinquent tax, and get the rate sheet for your district from the treasurer before you set a price.

faqs.q: What are the Union County due dates and penalties?
faqs.a: Mid-February is typical for the first half, with the second half falling between mid-July and August. The treasurer announces exact dates yearly; for tax year 2025 they were February 18 and August 12, 2026.

faqs.q: What penalty applies to a late Union County tax payment?
faqs.a: Under the 2026 schedule, a 5 percent penalty hit the day after each due date and rose to 10 percent ten days later. Interest on older delinquent tax followed on September 1, with another charge on December 1.

faqs.q: How do I appeal my Union County property value?
faqs.a: Send a notarized Board of Revision complaint to the Auditor's Office, 233 West Sixth Street in Marysville, by email, fax or mail. The filing period runs January 1 through March 31 after the tax year ends.

faqs.q: Can I pay my Union County taxes monthly?
faqs.a: Yes. The Real Estate Tax Escrow Program lets you prepay on a monthly basis, and the treasurer applies the funds when each half comes due. Contact the treasurer's office to enroll.

faqs.q: Who pays the property tax when a Union County home sells?
faqs.a: At closing the tax is usually split between the two parties by date. Once the sale closes, the buyer owes whatever comes due next. A bill that still reaches the former owner can be passed to the buyer, or the treasurer can issue a fresh one.
